title: Design System: landing-forge, «El muro de la casa»

display.purpose: Hero headline painted on the wall; highlight switches to neon script.

title.purpose: Wall-label titles, menu items, framed sign titles.

neon.purpose: Lit signage only; size set per placement.

shadows.name: sign-plate
shadows.purpose: Acrylic plate behind a neon sign.

shadows.name: gilt-rules
shadows.purpose: Flat stepped rules of the gold frame, combined with hung-object.

shadows.name: neon-glow
shadows.value: 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--c-neon) 30%, white), 0 0 10px var(--c-neon), 0 0 24px var(--c-neon), 0 0 48px color-mix(in oklab, var(--c-neon) 70%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: text-shadow: the light of the neon tube.

shadows.name: molding
shadows.purpose: Wood rail where brick meets flat paint; casts onto the section below.

motion.name: ease-hang
motion.purpose: Frames straighten (rotate to 0) and lift 4px over 0.6s on hover or focus.

motion.name: ignite
motion.purpose: Neon sign flickers on once at load, only when JS is present.

variableTokens.note: wall and neon are resolved at build time per business from data/<slug>/brand.json, else the business.json palette (neon falls back to palette.accent), and set as --c-wall/--c-neon on <html>. Defaults #5c2a20 / #ff4fa3. Optional wall_texture "brick" derives a drawn brick tile from the same wall value at build time.

wallTexture.placement: Brick wraps the hero band and replaces wall-deep on the closing section; a molding sits after the hero and before the closing. Middle sections and footer stay flat paint.
wallTexture.generator: site/src/lib/brick.ts brickTile(wall, seedFrom(slug)) -> SVG data URL

tile.bond: running (half-brick offset on alternate courses), seamless

derivation.chip: ~12% of bricks, 9x6px top corner in mortar

wallTexture.determinism: Seeded from the business slug (seedFrom): stable per business, different brick layout and colour between businesses.

narrative.overview:
The page is the business's own salon wall. Every section is flat paint in the business's wall colour; on it hang the business's photographs in mismatched frames (gilt, matte black, plaster mats), museum wall labels beside them, brass plaques for labels and actions, and the business's name or key phrase lit as a neon sign. Nothing is a card on a canvas: everything is an object hung on a wall, so everything casts a soft shadow onto the paint and sits a little askew until the visitor reaches for it.

The world is per-business. Two tokens, **wall** and **neon**, are variable: they are resolved at build time from `data/<slug>/brand.json` (observed brand colours, which win) or from the automatic palette in `business.json`, and injected as `--c-wall` / `--c-neon` on `<html>`. The hex values in the frontmatter are the defaults and La Gatoria's values (`#5c2a20` brick, `#ff4fa3` pink). Every other material (gilt, brass, plaster, frame black, engrave) is fixed, because real frames and plaques look the same on any wall. **wall-deep** and **chalk** are derived from the wall by mixing, so they shift with it.

The wall has one optional second material. When `brand.json` sets `"wall_texture": "brick"`, the opening (hero) and the close sit on a drawn running-bond brick wall generated from the same wall colour, and a dark wood molding with a gilt fillet marks each place where brick meets the flat paint that carries the middle sections. Brick is drawn, not photographed: a vector tile of flat-toned bricks with flat edge strips, so it stays as flat as the paint. Without the flag the whole page is flat paint, exactly as before.

Density is gallery-like rather than grid-like: a 12-column container at 1360px with asymmetric spans, generous vertical rhythm, and photographs carrying the proof. This is the pipeline's default template. Two other templates render the same `business.json` but sit outside this system: «clasica» (the earlier pre-Impeccable template) and «cuarto-oscuro» (an unfinished experiment). Nothing here describes them.
keyCharacteristics: Flat painted wall owns every section; depth comes from hung objects and their shadows, never gradients.
Optional drawn brick (flag-driven) for the opening and the close, derived from the wall colour, divided from the paint by a wood-and-gilt molding.
Three frame materials (gilt with flat gold rules, matte black, plaster mat) mixed on purpose, never uniform.
Brass plaques with engraved dark text for primary actions, rating, and hours.
One neon colour, used only as lit signage in Yellowtail script.
Slight tilt at rest, straighten and lift on hover or focus; the neon ignites once on load.
Square corners everywhere; the only round shapes are screw heads.

rules.name: The Wall Owns Everything Rule
rules.body: Every section background is the wall, in one of two materials: flat paint (wall or wall-deep) everywhere, or, when the business opts in, drawn brick for the opening and the close with flat paint between. Light surfaces exist only as objects hung on it (mats, labels, framed notes), never as full-bleed bands.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Neon appears only as lit signage text (headline highlight, handle sign, story sign, closing line) and as selection. Never on buttons, borders, icons, or fills.

rules.name: The Variable Paint Rule
rules.body: Never hard-code a wall or neon value in a component; read `--c-wall` / `--c-neon` (or the derived tokens) so each business's colours land everywhere. The brick tile is the one build-time derivation: it is generated from the same resolved wall value, so it shifts with the business too.

rules.name: The Script Is Light Rule
rules.body: Yellowtail is used only with the neon treatment. Never set reading text, labels, or buttons in it.

rules.name: The Display Is One Weight Rule
rules.body: Gloock runs at 400 everywhere; hierarchy comes from size, not weight.

rules.name: The Nothing Floats Rule
rules.body: Every object on the wall carries a soft drop shadow; a light surface without one reads as a card, which this world does not have.

rules.name: The Flat Gold Rule
rules.body: Gilt frames are built from flat stepped rules (inset and outset rings in gilt-dark and gilt-light), never gradients or bevel images.

rules.name: The Drawn Brick Rule
rules.body: Brick is a flat plane like the paint: per-brick flat tones with flat edge strips, drawn in vector from the wall colour. No gradients, no photographic or raster texture, no shadow cast by the brick itself.

dos: **Do** read wall and neon from `--c-wall` / `--c-neon` and derive deeper or lighter steps with `color-mix(in oklab, ...)`.
**Do** hang every photograph in a frame, mixing gilt, black and matted frames, with a small rest tilt and the hung-object shadow.
**Do** use the brass plaque for the primary action and the plaster outline plaque for the secondary one.
**Do** keep the motion grammar to one ignition and one straighten; under reduced motion show the sign lit and frames still.
**Do** quote reviews literally inside framed notes, with author and date beneath a 1px rule.
**Do** enable brick only through the `wall_texture` flag, keep it to the opening and the close, and put a molding at every brick-to-paint edge.
donts: **Don't** use neon for anything but lit signage and selection.
**Don't** set reading text, labels or buttons in Yellowtail.
**Don't** round corners on frames, plaques, labels or tags.
**Don't** build gilt from gradients or put gradients on the wall.
**Don't** place a light surface on the wall without a drop shadow, or tile photos in rows of equal unframed cards.
**Don't** hard-code a business's wall or neon hex in a component.
**Don't** use a photographed or raster brick texture, or shade brick with gradients; generate it from the wall colour.
**Don't** run brick behind the middle sections or butt brick against paint without a molding.
